verdict.rationale: The docs show record deletion via `table.delete(...)`. They also document reindexing, including incremental indexing of updated data via `optimize()`, so the product has its own mutation and index-refresh path. However, the pack never shows an upsert/merge operation and never documents how quickly writes become visible in search or what consistency guarantees readers get. missing for 10: documented upsert/merge-insert, documented freshness/read-consistency semantics, evidence of continuous-write visibility latency, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can upsert and delete records continuously and have changes reflected in search results quickly, with documented freshness/consistency behavior

citations.quote: You can manually trigger an incremental indexing operation on updated data using the `optimize()` method on a table.
Reindexing is the process of updating the index to account for new data -- this applies to either a full-text search (FTS) index or a vector index.
